title: Case split on the exponent n for IMO 1961 Q3 (forward direction)
intent: In the forward direction of IMO 1961 Q3, after the degenerate cases sin x = 0 and cos x = 0 are discharged, the remaining branch (sin x ≠ 0 and cos x ≠ 0) is shown contradictory for every n ≥ 1 by a match on n: two small exceptional cases n = 1 and n = 2 close by direct rewriting, and the residual n = m + 2 closes by one uniform bound using |cos x| < 1 and |sin x| < 1.

parent.name: Imo1961Q3_forward
parent.statement: (cos x) ^ n - (sin x) ^ n = 1 → (∃ k : ℤ, k * π = x) ∧ Even n ∨ (∃ k : ℤ, k * (2 * π) = x) ∧ Odd n ∨ (∃ k : ℤ, -(π / 2) + k * (2 * π) = x) ∧ Odd n   [premise h₀ : n ≠ 0]

children.name: case n = 1
children.statement: goal after `| 1 =>`; rewriting h to `cos x = sin x + 1` and using `cos_sq_add_sin_sq x` forces `2 * sin x * cos x = 0`, which contradicts `hsinx` and `hcosx`
children.closed_by: rw [pow_one, pow_one, sub_eq_iff_eq_add] at h; have : 2 * sin x * cos x = 0 := by simpa [h, add_sq, add_assoc, ← two_mul, mul_add, mul_assoc, ← sq] using cos_sq_add_sin_sq x; simp [hsinx, hcosx] at this

children.name: case n = 2
children.statement: goal after `| 2 =>`; rewriting h via `cos_sq_add_sin_sq` reduces it to `sin x = 0`, contradicting `hsinx`
children.closed_by: rw [← cos_sq_add_sin_sq x, sub_eq_add_neg, add_right_inj, neg_eq_self] at h; exact absurd (eq_zero_of_pow_eq_zero h) hsinx

children.name: residual n = m + 2
children.statement: goal after `| (n + 1 + 2) =>`; `set m := n + 1` writes the exponent as `m + 2`, and a `calc` chain proves `(cos x)^(m+2) - (sin x)^(m+2) < 1`, contradicting `h` (which says it equals 1)
children.closed_by: set m := n + 1; refine absurd ?_ h.not_lt; calc … ≤ … = … < … = 1 (the two `gcongr` steps use hcos1 : |cos x| < 1 and hsin1 : |sin x| < 1)

applicability.goal_shape: A goal about `n : ℕ` (here the forward direction `(cos x)^n - (sin x)^n = 1 → …`) whose truth depends on `n` only through which small numerals `n` equals and a residual `n ≥ 3` that admits one uniform argument; the small cases are exceptional and the residual case is where a monotonic/decay bound takes over.
applicability.use_when: the exceptional cases (`n = 1`, `n = 2`) close by short, separate rewrites, while every larger `n` shares one argument (here powers of `|cos x|` and `|sin x|` shrink because `|cos x| < 1` and `|sin x| < 1`); the split's residual pattern is written `n + 1 + 2` (an offset successor pattern), which Lean elaborates as `n + 3`.
applicability.avoid_when: the residual case genuinely needs induction (then the recursion, not a one-shot bound, is the content); the cases do not share a residual argument; or the domain includes `n = 0` with no hypothesis excluding it, so you need an explicit `0` branch.

claims.claim: The `match n with` at lines 51-71 has exactly three branches — `| 1 =>` (52-57), `| 2 =>` (58-60), `| (n + 1 + 2) =>` (61-71) — and each closes on its own: `simp [hsinx, hcosx] at this` (line 57), `exact absurd (eq_zero_of_pow_eq_zero h) hsinx` (line 60), and `refine absurd ?_ h.not_lt` with a `calc` chain ending in `< 1` (lines 63-71).

The match has no `| 0 =>` branch: its three branches `1`, `2`, `n + 1 + 2` cover exactly `n ≥ 1`, matching the premise `h₀ : n ≠ 0` (line 26), so exhaustiveness is carried by the premise rather than by a separate `0` child or an exhaustiveness lemma.

The residual branch reuses the two strict bounds `hcos1 : |cos x| < 1` and `hsin1 : |sin x| < 1` (lines 45-50) in its two `gcongr` steps (lines 67 and 70), which is what makes the `calc` chain strictly decreasing rather than merely `≤`.
The authors state that the solution follows an external write-up: 'The solution is based on the one at the Art of Problem Solving website' (file header).
The three match branches are 6, 3 and 11 lines long, so the residual case is the bulk of the proof and the two small cases are one-liner rewrites.

metrics.how_counted: parent site = lines 51-71 of the copied file; children = the three match branches at lines 52-57, 58-60 and 61-71

consequences: The `match` creates three goals. There is no `0` branch: exhaustiveness of the split over `n ≥ 1` rests on the premise `h₀ : n ≠ 0` (line 26), so a `0` goal never appears as a child. The residual branch introduces a fresh `n` (the pattern variable in `n + 1 + 2`) and renames it `set m := n + 1`, so the exponent is written `m + 2` before the bound is applied; forgetting that renaming breaks the head of the `calc` chain. The residual argument depends on the two strict bounds `|cos x| < 1` and `|sin x| < 1` (lines 45-50): with only `≤ 1` the `<` link would fail and the split would not close, so those bounds are a hidden obligation of this move.
